summary.text: Larry Rhoden is the Republican Governor of South Dakota and the party's nominee for a first full term. A West River rancher, he served in the Legislature and as lieutenant governor under Kristi Noem before succeeding her in January 2025.
He is running on keeping the state "strong, safe, and free," and names property tax cuts, defense manufacturing and rural health care among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Rhoden was born on February 5, 1959, in Sturgis and raised on a farm.
He graduated from Sunshine Bible Academy in 1977 and served in the South Dakota National Guard from 1978 to 1985.

While his children were young he served as a church trustee and on the local school board and led the board of directors for the area Cenex; he is a deacon of his home church, still does custom welding and operates the ranch where he was born.
Rhoden was elected to the state House in 2000 and served there from 2001 to 2009, including four years as majority leader.
After he was term-limited, he served in the state Senate from 2009 to 2015, and he lost the 2014 Republican U.S. Senate primary to Mike Rounds.
He returned to the House in 2017 and served until 2019.
His office's biography says he chaired both the Senate and House State Affairs committees and worked with then-Representative Noem on property tax reform.
In June 2018 Kristi Noem chose Rhoden as her running mate, and they were elected that November; they were re-elected in 2022.
He served as lieutenant governor from January 2019 and as interim secretary of agriculture in 2020, then as South Dakota's Agriculture Ambassador from 2020 to 2025.
He became the 34th governor on January 25, 2025, when Noem resigned to become U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security, and he later chose Tony Venhuizen as lieutenant governor.

As governor, Rhoden signed a pair of property tax relief bills on March 12, 2026, SB 96 and SB 245, which supporters called the largest property tax cut in state history and critics called a tax shift onto sales tax.
He announced his 2026 candidacy in November 2025 and won the Republican nomination in South Dakota's first primary runoff, defeating Toby Doeden on July 28 with 70.8% of the vote.

In a September 2026 interview, he cited the state's Data Center Bill of Rights and a new women's correctional facility in Pierre, and listed expanding defense manufacturing through the South Dakota Defense Institute, property tax cuts and rural health care as top priorities.
Rhoden and his wife, Sandy, have four sons and ten grandchildren.
